standard_prerequisites: The length of a quasi-coherent module at a point, and its compatibility with etale charts
Etale charts and the cartesian description of the points of a fibre product, together with stability of closed immersions under base change

The identification of the pushforward along a base changed closed immersion with the restriction of the pushforward, and the algebra statement that the length of a module over a local ring agrees with its length viewed through a surjection of local rings
core_obligations: Choose an etale chart of the target through which the given point factors, form the fibre product with the closed subspace, and record that the induced morphism to the chart is again a closed immersion
Identify the restriction of the pushforward of the module with the pushforward of the restricted module along that closed immersion of schemes, thereby reducing the statement to the case of schemes

In the scheme case compute the stalk of the pushforward at the point as the stalk of the module at the corresponding point, with its module structure induced by the surjection of local rings, and conclude equality of lengths by the algebra statement
proof_roadmap: Reduce to schemes by an etale chart and the resulting base changed closed immersion
Identify the two stalks in the scheme case and compare lengths through the surjection of local rings
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the invariance of the length at a point under pushforward along a closed immersion at source lines 520-531, label lemma-length-closed-immersion, whose proof occupies source lines 533-556. The proof reduces the statement about algebraic spaces to the case of schemes by choosing an etale chart of the target, forming the fibre product with the closed subspace and identifying the restriction of the pushforward with the pushforward of the restricted module along the induced closed immersion, which is where the base change compatibility of pushforwards is used. In the scheme case the two stalks are identified as modules over the local ring of the target through the surjection of local rings, and the equality of lengths follows from the algebra statement that length is insensitive to that presentation. The counted statement records neither the chart reduction nor the stalk identification.
